Meeting header: 2026-03-05 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Maya, Diego (Redwood) - Liam, Priya, Evan (Oxford Capital)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, joined by Diego from our infra team. How are you all?
[00:06] Liam: Good thanks, sorry for the slight delay on our end, had a back-to-back.
[00:09] Priya: Hi all, Priya here.
[00:11] Evan: Evan - SecOps.
[00:13] Diego: Hey! quick wave.
[00:15] Maya: Quick agenda - we wanna understand your usage patterns, budget, and then walk through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private economics and practical levers like batching and KV/prefix caching that change per-token unit cost. Does that work?
[00:24] Liam: Yes, perfect. We're trying to figure whether to go hosted initially or commit to dedicated capacity; our CFO set a soft cap of about twenty thousand USD a month for the first pilot.
[00:34] Priya: And from an engineering POV, we care about 95th p90 latency < 200ms for short completions and throughput for larger batch scoring jobs overnight.
[00:43] Diego: Great - can I ask about request profile? Are you doing many short chat-like calls or long generation, or both?
[00:49] Priya: Mostly both. Real-time assistant for traders with short prompts (~50-80 tokens) and nightly batch embeddings and reranks - those can be up to 2048 tokens per example but run in bulk.
[00:59] Liam: Also we care about data retention - nothing leaves our VPC for the POC ideally, but we can be flexible if hosted isolation is strong.
[01:07] Evan: Specifically SSO/SAML integration and KMS for keys, audit logs, and SOC2 type stuff.
[01:13] Maya: Totally. We support SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration for Private. Hosted also has strong controls but Dedicated/Private give you more isolation. For the economics piece - our Hosted pricing is per-token with tiered volume discounts; Dedicated is an instance-based model (reserved GPU capacity) that maps to a per-token effective cost depending on utilization.
[01:30] Diego: To add, the key levers you'll use are batching, prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, and maybe quantized model variants for lower-cost inference. Those together can drop your effective per-token cost by 2-6x depending on workload.
[01:45] Priya: When you say prefix caching, is that the same as KV cache or something separate?
[01:49] Diego: They're similar - KV cache stores activations for previous tokens to avoid recomputing on follow-up, prefix caching is more about reusing the same prompt prefixes across requests. Both reduce compute per request.
[01:59] Liam: Can you give a concrete example of numbers, say for a 50-token chat call?
[02:03] Maya: Sure - rough Hosted list price for a 50-token chat completion might be $0.0006 per 1k tokens for input and $0.0020 per 1k tokens for output - so that 50 token completion is effectively pennies. But those numbers depend on model size; I'm throwing typical figures. For Dedicated the math flips: you reserve capacity - say a 8-GPU pool - which costs X per hour, but if you're fully utilized the per-token cost drops below hosted. The crossover depends on utilization.
[02:27] Priya: Ok - our expected pilot traffic is ~300k short chat tokens/day plus a nightly batch of 1M tokens for embeddings and reranks. That's about 10M tokens month? rough.
[02:40] Diego: With that profile you might be near the breakpoint where Dedicated makes sense if you can commit and keep high utilization. If utilization is spiky, Hosted with autoscaling or a small Dedicated reserve plus burst may be better.
[02:51] Evan: Our budget again is ~20k/month for pilot - can you help show how that maps to latency/throughput we can expect?
[02:59] Maya: Absolutely - we'll send a worked example but roughly: on Hosted with recommended model variants and batching, 20k could give you X throughput with p95 under 200ms for small completions; with Dedicated you could get lower unit costs but need to commit to the monthly reserved price which might be higher upfront.
[03:14] Liam: Can you clarify the burst capacity - we have unpredictable spikes in market events; if dedicated is saturated do you fallback to hosted?
[03:21] Diego: Yes - smart routing can fail over to hosted or another region/pool. We support hybrid routing policies so you can reserve capacity and allow overflow to hosted at a set priority and cost.
[03:31] Priya: On batching - there's a tension for us: we need low latency for the trader assistant, but batching helps for embeddings. How much does batching help?
[03:38] Diego: For CPU/GPU kernels batching increases GPU utilization; for large models you can get 2-4x throughput improvements for batch scoring versus single-shot inference. For embeddings, batching is huge - the per-example cost drops significantly.
[03:48] Maya: Example: if a single request might cost $0.0005 tokens at small batch, batching to 8-16 could drop the effective per-example compute to a fraction. We'll include a table in the workbook.
[03:57] Evan: Any differences across models? Like smaller quantized vs full fp16?
[04:01] Diego: Absolutely - quantized 4-bit models can cut memory and compute and cost, but they may change quality. For reranks/embeds often quantized models are fine. For the trader assistant you might want fp16 for best quality; but we've seen quantized LLMs that maintain acceptable latency/quality tradeoffs.
[04:17] Liam: How about caching - can we cache user-specific prefixes? We have many users with similar prompts.
[04:22] Diego: Yes - prefix caching at the KV level is supported. If your prefix is identical across requests the runtime can reuse the KV state and only compute the delta which saves tokens and compute. That really helps for chat use-cases.
[04:33] Priya: Does Hosted store those keys outside our VPC? Any data retention concerns?
[04:37] Maya: Hosted keeps customer data isolated but for strict requirements Private or Dedicated (VPC peering / on-prem) is recommended. We can also do customer-managed KMS with Dedicated/Private.
[04:46] Evan: On SOC2 and audit logs - Hosted has SOC2 Type II and we can provide details?
[04:50] Maya: Yes, we can share our compliance pack. For on-prem Private you'll own the logs entirely.
[04:56] Liam: Back to unit economics - you mentioned a 2-6x reduction with batching/caching. What do your customers see moving from hosted to dedicated typically?
[05:04] Diego: It varies - typical savings are 1.5-3x on per-token cost once you hit steady-state for Dedicated compared to Hosted list prices, and combined with caching and batching you can see overall 3-6x. But if utilization is low you could pay more because of reserved capacity.
[05:19] Priya: Can you show an example with our numbers? 10M tokens/month estimate and 20k budget.
[05:25] Maya: Quick back-of-envelope: if Hosted effective blended rate is $0.0003 per token (depending on model mix), 10M tokens -> $3k. That seems low - I need to clarify: those per-token rates are per-1k token units, so double-checking, sorry there's confusion. Let's be explicit in the spreadsheet.
[05:40] Liam: No worries - we need transparent math. CFO wants to understand worst-case for spikes as well.
[05:45] Diego: We'll include a few scenarios: low-utilization hosted, mid-utilization hybrid, and committed dedicated at various utilizations. Also include reserved GPU hourly $ numbers so you see the fixed vs variable tradeoffs.
[05:58] Priya: Regarding monitoring - can we get token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards?
[06:02] Maya: Yes Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. You'll be able to see cost per model, per-route, and per-identity if you want.
[06:12] Evan: For the security review - our security team needs an initial checklist. I'll share our internal standard and we can map gaps.
[06:18] Evan: (overlapping) e.g., we need private networking, KMS integration, audit retention 12 months.
[06:23] Maya: Understood - Diego will follow up on technical specifics.
[06:26] Diego: On the VPC/private side, we support VPC Peering and private control plane for Dedicated/Private, and on-prem options for air-gapped if needed. There's a deployment checklist we'll share.
[06:36] Liam: One more question: what about model rollouts and canarying? We want to test a new model variant without affecting traders.
[06:41] Diego: The rollout tooling supports canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can route small percent traffic to a new model and fallback to previous on error.
[06:50] Priya: Great. Are there any hidden costs - e.g., networking, storage for cache, or logs?
[06:55] Maya: Good question - storage and logs for Hosted are included up to typical retention; longer retention or S3 export might incur extra. Network egress costs depend on region and deployment; Dedicated on cloud you'd still pay normal cloud egress. We'll enumerate those.
[07:07] Liam: How quickly can we run a benchmark? We want to replicate our overnight rerank job and a few low-latency flows.
[07:12] Maya: We can spin up a small pilot - Diego can share a bench harness and we can run both Hosted and Dedicated comparisons. How soon can you provide sample prompt sets and datasets?
[07:21] Priya: We can assemble a small set in a few days; say by Monday 2026-03-09.
[07:26] Maya: Perfect, we'll target running benchmarks the week of 2026-03-09 and follow up with results.
[07:31] Evan: For procurement - what's the typical contract length for Dedicated?
[07:35] Maya: Dedicated is usually reserved monthly or annual commits. Monthly reserved can be shorter term but at a higher per-unit cost compared to annual commitments which offer discounts.
[07:43] Liam: Ok. Can we discuss some specific numbers - Diego, can you share typical GPU pool hourly for a 8-GPU pool?
[07:50] Diego: Roughly, depending on cloud/hardware, an 8xA100 style pool might be in the $X00-$Y00 per hour range for reserved, but I'll provide the exact range in the deck - sorry not to throw raw numbers here. We try not to mislead with placeholders.
[08:05] Priya: Understood. I just want to flag our latency SLA - if we go Dedicated we need 99.9% uptime and p95 latency under 200ms; is that supported?
[08:13] Diego: Yes we offer SLA-backed targets for Dedicated and can align to those in the contract. For hosted we have best-effort with good reliability but not the same SLA.
[08:22] Liam: For the overflow routing, is there price transparency when traffic overflows to hosted?
[08:27] Maya: Yes, the routing policy includes an overflow rate and the cost will be charged at Hosted rates for overflow traffic; we'll show sample cost implications in the workbook.
[08:35] Priya: Are there tooling integrations for observability - like Grafana/Prometheus export?
[08:39] Diego: We have metrics exports and integrations - logs, traces and metrics can be exported to your existing stack.
[08:45] Evan: Any known limitations around KV cache size per instance?
[08:49] Diego: There's practical limits depending on model and GPU memory, we shard and manage KV cache; for very large numbers of concurrent unique prefixes you might need to size accordingly. We'll include sizing guidance.
[08:59] Maya: Cool - let's recap next steps. We're gonna send pricing worksheet, bench harness, security/compliance pack, and schedule the benchmark week of 3/9. Any objections?
[09:10] Liam: Sounds good.
[09:12] Priya: No objections.
[09:13] Evan: Good.
[09:15] Maya: Awesome thanks everyone - we'll follow up in email and confirm the benchmark slots.
[09:20] --END OF CALL--
